title: Pack six eggs point-down from an egg flat into a half-dozen carton and close its lid
instruction: Pack all six eggs from the egg flat into the carton, one to a cell, pointed end down, without cracking any, and close the lid.
context: Packing eggs into a carton is something nearly everyone has done at a kitchen counter or a farm stall: stand each egg in its own cell, pointed end down, without a knock, then close the lid. An egg dropped or knocked hard cracks, one left standing high keeps the lid from shutting, and a lid forced over it splits the shell. The job is done when the lid is shut on six whole eggs standing in the six cells and the hands are off.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) Carton: half-dozen (2 x 3) moulded-pulp egg carton, grey-brown, 108 x 160 mm, 34 mm to the rim, 72 mm closed, 2 mm walls; each cell a square funnel 52 mm across at the rim, 20 mm at the floor, 32 mm deep (sizes est from a typical 6-count carton; measure yours). It stands in a fixed pack-out cradle (four 6 mm rails round its foot), long side along y, centred x 260 mm, y +50 mm. Cell centres (x, y) mm: (234, -2), (234, 50), (234, 102), (286, -2), (286, 50), (286, 102). Its lid, 111 mm deep, 36 mm clear inside, hinged along the near long side (x 206 mm, 34 mm up), stands open at 110 degrees against its hinge stop, leaning back toward the arms; closed it sits on the carton. (2) Egg flat: a 30-pocket moulded flat, 255 x 306 mm, pockets 51 mm apart, 30 mm deep, centred x 300, y +295 mm; rows at x 198 to 402 mm, columns at y 167.5 to 422.5 mm. Six USDA large eggs, white, 57 g, 57 mm long x 44 mm wide, stand pointed end down in it at (x, y) mm: (249, 371.5), (300, 371.5), (351, 371.5), (249, 218.5), (300, 218.5), (351, 218.5); the other 24 pockets are empty. A seated egg's blunt end stands 28 mm over the carton rim. Eggs: store at 4 C in their own carton, take out 30 to 60 min before the trial so they are dry and at room temperature (20 to 22 C), use the same day, handle by hand only; for a rig-safe run use shell-on hard-boiled eggs (12 min, cooled, dried), preferred over ceramic eggs, which do not show a crack. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step. Seated: an egg's centre within 12 mm of a cell centre (top view), its blunt end no more than 6 mm higher than a fully seated egg's (a straightedge across the rim), and its long axis within 25 degrees of vertical with the pointed end down; one egg per cell. Lid closed: the lid's free edge within 5 mm of the carton rim at its closed place. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the carton, lid and eggs, and over that 1 s nothing visibly moves: no egg moves more than 5 mm or turns more than 5 degrees, and the lid turns no more than 5 degrees. Score 0 if any egg cracks or the hands-off check fails (it gates every tier). Otherwise: 1.0 six seated, lid closed, hands off; 0.75 six seated, lid not closed; 0.5 four or five seated; 0.25 one to three; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: seated, a look from above, a ruler and a straightedge across the rim, and a 25 degree protractor on each egg; lid, a 5 mm feeler at its free edge; crack, candling each egg or a check of the shell and carton for a crack or leak; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand and 30 fps video of the last 1 s showing no visible movement (a 5 mm mark on the carton and a 5 degree card; eggs inside the closed carton are judged by the carton and lid, and after the trial lift the lid to check the eggs; the sim reads the same 5 mm and 5 degrees).
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Each egg is 12 stacked discs turned on its axis (44 x 57 mm, 57 g, blunt end larger); pulp, cells and lid are rigid, the carton fixed in its cradle, the lid a hinge with a stop (a real lid has a tab and flexes). A crack is a declared rule: an egg moving at 0.8 m/s or more (a fall of about 33 mm, or a throw) or lost off the table. Shell strength and grip force are not simulated. Sizes, friction (0.45 shell, 0.50 pulp) and lid damping are estimates.
reset_notes: Stand six fresh eggs (4 C fridge stock, out 30 to 60 min, room temperature) pointed end down in the flat's pockets listed, empty the carton, open its lid to the 110 degree stop and seat the carton in its cradle. Discard any cracked or dropped egg and use a fresh one: a real trial uses six fresh eggs per run. Wipe up a break at once and clean the pads with a damp cloth; shell-on hard-boiled eggs spare the rig.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (run under the same 5 mm and 5 degree stillness check; relaxing it cannot lower the score)
